Executor order: detect VSX first (vsx stat -v, by text per CF-4), then choose the physical form, then per-VS reads.

CheckPointIpRouteParser: numeric proto tokens; 7 -> PROTOCOL_STATIC, kernel -> PROTOCOL_CONNECTED, other numerics -> PROTOCOL_UNKNOWN; 'dev X proto 7 scope link' without src parsed as a route; table local rows dropped (fixture from the measured shapes, 22 lines / 6 routes and 13 lines / 3 routes).

CheckPointIpAddrParser: '@ifNN' parent form and 'link-netnsid' trailer tolerated; 'vlan protocol 802.1Q id N' detail line read into the VLAN id when present; fixture with a bond VLAN subinterface and a VS-context subinterface.

CheckPointClusterVirtualInterfaceParser: 'vsid N:' header tolerated; rows with 'VMAC address:' trailer; both VLAN table shapes ignored; per-VS output produces cluster_virtual addresses attributed to that VS context (executor wiring).

CheckPointHaStateParser: the two measured mode strings; the VSLS 'Virtual Devices Status on each Cluster Member' table parsed into per-VSID role for the local member ([local] column) -- expose it on the parser result; persistence of HA role is out of scope unless a column already exists (it does not; leave a TODO-free note in the SESSION_CLOSE instead).
CheckPointVsxStatParser: 'VSX is not supported on this platform' -> not VSX (empty, flagged); rows parsed by the ID column with the type letter kept; VS0 excluded by the caller as today.
All CP parsers: unknown/interleaved lines (e.g. 'Message from syslogd@...' and kernel lines) skipped and counted, never fatal; one fixture per parser carrying such a line.
Fixtures use RFC 5737 addresses and made-up names (no estate value); every fixture mirrors a measured shape from the findings document.
